Import

Bring your Splitwise CSV into an itemized ledger.

Trezzit migration is a guided CSV flow, not a vague connector claim. It maps people, handles placeholders, recognizes settlement rows, and verifies the resulting balances before the import sticks.

Upload, Group, You, Map, Done.

01

Upload

Drop in a Splitwise CSV export with Date, Description, Category, Cost, Currency, and per-person columns.

02

Group

Create a new Trezzit group or choose the destination group for the imported ledger.

03

You

Trezzit suggests the likely current user by checking "You", full name, then first name.

04

Map

Match CSV people to Trezzit people, or create placeholder members for names not in the group yet.

05

Done

Review the result, invite placeholders, and keep the imported balances only if verification passes.

Ground truth

Five migration claims we can stand behind.

Recognizes Splitwise CSV exports

Trezzit handles Splitwise export headers and Splitwise-specific rows like Total balance and Settle all balances.

Auto-detects who you are

The You step tries literal "You", then full name, then first name, and shows a likely-you suggestion.

Unknown names become invitable placeholders

New CSV names can become placeholder members, with invite links generated after import.

Balance-verified, all-or-nothing imports

After bill creation, Trezzit recomputes balances and rolls back if they miss Splitwise totals by more than one cent.

Settlement-aware

Settlement-looking rows become first-class payment records instead of fake bills.

Boundary

No exchange-rate guessing.

Trezzit groups lock currency at creation. The import reads the CSV currency column, but this page avoids cross-currency migration claims because balance verification is only safe when the export is effectively one currency.
